physicalNotes: Radius 1.1 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since HD 39091 b does not transit, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html): 78,641.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 14.1 Jupiter masses (Damasso et al. 2020, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...642A..31D/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Damasso et al. 2020 (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL__2020): P 2088.8 d
sources.shape: Damasso et al. 2020 (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL__2020): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 3.28 au and stellar radius 1.17 solar radii; inclination 45.8 +1.4 degrees, measured in the same fit
sources.eccentricity: Damasso et al. 2020 (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL__2020): e 0.642
sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: Damasso et al. 2020 (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL__2020): omega -30.1 degrees, stored as 329.9
sources.phase: Damasso et al. 2020 (2020A&A...642A..31D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL__2020): periastron passage 2458388.6 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB
sources.orientation: Display convention: the NASA Exoplanet Archive carries no position angle for the orbit's node on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
